I will still do it much like last year, just watch the sky and the money a bit tighter. I have only 8 mu, so I cannot gamble. Maize is the crop that brings the main grain, so I will put more land, more fertilizer, and more water on maize. If maize goes wrong, the whole year feels bad. Mungbean costs less and does not eat much fertilizer, so I will keep a smaller piece for it. I do what I have seen work around me: for maize I use hybrid seed, put the base fertilizer in before sowing, then topdress once when the plants are knee high to waist high. I would rather give maize a bit more fertilizer than let the leaves turn pale and lose ears. Since I have well water, I will not let it suffer in the key time. For mungbean, I will not feed it heavy like maize. Too much nitrogen just makes stems and leaves. I will give it some phosphate and potash, keep the land clean, and spray when insects show up. I am 63 now, with only 2 people at home, so I will keep the work simple: rotary tillage, not too many field passes, and crop choices I already know how to handle.
